title: Katsina Bandits Reject Cash Ransom, Demand Prisoner Exchange for Abducted Retired General
detail: Bandit leader Kachallah Muhammad, who orchestrated the May 30 abduction of retired Major General Rabe Abubakar Batsari and his wife in Matazu LGA, Katsina State, formally rejected any cash ransom and demanded instead the release of jailed gang members from Nigerian prison custody. The demand, relayed through the family by June 3, represented an escalation in bandit negotiation tactics — shifting from purely financial demands to political prisoner-exchange conditions. Defence Headquarters confirmed awareness of the situation but did not disclose operational details. The case heightened national debate over the government's counterbanditry strategy in the Northwest and the apparent inability of security forces to prevent high-profile abductions.

media.caption: Katsina bandits demand prisoner exchange for abducted retired general and wife

title: NLC and TUC Threaten Strike in Anambra Over Unexplained Civil Service Salary Deductions
detail: The Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress convened an emergency meeting in Awka, Anambra State on June 3 to plan industrial action after the Anambra State Government began deducting ₦25,000–₦48,000 monthly from civil servants' salaries without explanation or legal basis. Labour leaders described the deductions as a violation of agreed pay structures and threatened an indefinite strike if the government did not reverse the policy within 72 hours. The Anambra dispute adds to a national pattern of worker-government tensions that saw the NLC demand a ₦154,000 national minimum wage and threaten action against both federal and state governments over cost-of-living failures.

media.caption: NLC and TUC threaten strike in Anambra over unlawful salary deductions from civil servants
